questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The mountains, the language and my personal relations in the area.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think that the MUI could have made a better job of providing all information on one platform (website) instead of sending multiple emails with many attachments in each containing all different kind of information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not get much. Was simply told to show up at a department (Gyn/obs) and never got an introduction to the department or in general how the clinical rotations work in this country or what I was expected to do. So didn't have a very comfortable start and it took quite some time before I started to figure out, how it was running at the department.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: No. Was super difficult. I ended up finding my place 3 days before arrival. Stressful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it's almost impossible to find something, if you are not able to show up beforehand and meet the people and see the place. I only could get mine, since I was in the area a few weeks prior to the exchange's start.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Caotic, multiple e-mails with long to do lists. Then other institutions send you e-mails requesting information and quite often they want the same documents you already send to the host
instiution.Would
be much better if all inormation and all registration was at one website, because I was never sure if I was missing something.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Well the International coordinator Frau Schlager from the MUI was always very helpful to answer my questions. So I am very happy wwith her and that she was available.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Went well.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think honestly that I would give them an overview quide on important inforamtion about the registration process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only did clinical rotations and the quality varies from department to department. 2 out of 3 departments did a good job.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3 months of clinical rotations, no end exam.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much alike but of course I didnt take ay classes so I wouldnt know about that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: 1 month at respectively Gyn/obs, emergency ward and orthopedics.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I can recommend doing "Notfall" as an clinical rotation at the MUI. Very exciting and something you otherwise won't experience on the medical study.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Only an registration fee at the university of approx 20 euros

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Publix transport is quite expensive. Prices are in general pretty much like in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Innsbruck is incredible locationwise and the people there have a great mindset. The place is full of opportunities in the mountains and lots of events happining in the city.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do the sport events in town. Skijump, trailrunning. Such a great and different experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Mountains, sport. Go to Treibhaus which is the cultural house. Ag great bar to hang out at but also with jazz nights and other cultural shows. Just great.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use the ESN.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language since there are many different dialects located in Innsbruck.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Austrians are just very easygoing and in Innsrcuk, active.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make sure to seek out other medical students in the department on the first day to gather information on the ways of the department and where you can go as a student. 
2. You get free lunch in the canteen as an Erasmus student.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Yes, you can use your student card to borrow books at the university library.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Improving my language skills.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Language skills due to the heavy mountain dialects in the area.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
